A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed and synthesized a novel series of 2-aminopyrazolopyridine Plk1 inhibitors, with the best compound having a Ki of 2 nM and an IC50 of 5 nM in cell-free assay.
we have identified a series of potent, ATP competitive Plk inhibitors that may have potential for the development of new anti-cancer agents.

The main takeaway from our work is that
2-amino pyrazolopyridine is a new chemical scaffold for the design of Plk inhibitors, and that the pyridine ring is a key element for binding to Plk1.
2-amino-3,5-disubstituted pyrazolopyridine derivatives can serve as Plk1 inhibitors with good potency and selectivity, and that these compounds are amenable to optimization.
the 2-amino pyrazolopyridine scaffold is a viable starting point for the development of Plk1 inhibitors.
